interface.name: onyrion_shell_unstable_v1

description.summary: experimental Onyrion shell control protocol

interface.description:
Experimental development protocol between Onyrion core and shell clients.
The compositor is the authoritative source of state. Clients must be able to reconstruct their state from a fresh snapshot after reconnecting.
This interface is unstable and may change incompatibly.

request.name: get_state

description.summary: request a complete current state snapshot

request.description:
The compositor replies with state_begin, zero or more workspace events, then, for version 2 clients, zero or more group and window events, followed by state_end.
The generation in state_begin and state_end identifies the snapshot.

request.name: merge_group

description.summary: merge a source group into a target group

request.description: Both groups must currently belong to the same workspace. The target group identity is preserved.

request.name: move_window_to_group

description.summary: move one window to another group

request.description: Source and target groups must currently belong to the same workspace.

description.summary: split one window from its group into a new tile

request.name: move_window_range

description.summary: move a contiguous ordered window range

request.description: first_window_id must precede last_window_id in the same source group. The target group must be in that workspace.

description.summary: move a stable group to an available workspace

request.name: move_window_to_workspace

description.summary: move one window to an available workspace

request.description: The window joins that workspace active group, creating one when needed.

event.name: window_placement

description.summary: authoritative window placement relation

event.description: Publishes a managed window's direct workspace ownership, placement role, and optional parent window relation. A transient window is not an ordinary Group tab and therefore has an empty group_id in the legacy window event.

request.name: split_group_at

description.summary: split a group at an ordered window boundary

request.description: The window identifies both the source group and the first window of the new suffix group. The prefix must remain non-empty. The new Group is inserted adjacent to the source tile with the requested split orientation.

request.name: float_window

description.summary: detach a window into a floating Group

request.description: Compatibility request. A multi-tab source detaches this window into its own Group; a one-window source keeps its Group identity. The resulting Group owns floating geometry.

request.name: tile_window

description.summary: return a floating window to tiled placement

request.description: Compatibility request. A multi-tab floating Group detaches this window into its own tiled Group; a one-window floating Group keeps its Group identity and becomes tiled.

description.summary: authoritative Group placement and pin state
place a whole Group in floating placement
return a whole floating Group to tiled placement

request.name: set_group_pinned

description.summary: set output-local sticky state for a floating Group

request.description: Pinning is valid only for floating Groups. While pinned, the Group follows workspace changes only on the output where pinning occurred.

request.name: get_group_surface

description.summary: assign a Shell-owned wl_surface to a Group

request.description: The surface receives a lifetime role but its relative placement is entirely supplied by the Shell through onyrion_group_surface_v1. Creating the surface does not reserve client content geometry.

request.name: set_group_content_insets

description.summary: set Shell-defined Group client-content exclusions

request.description: Insets are independent from attached surface placement. Once set by a Shell resource, legacy 24px Core chrome is disabled for that Group. Destroying the owning Shell resource clears the insets and restores legacy fallback chrome.

description.summary: activate the next window in the active Group
activate the previous window in the active Group

request.name: begin_window_drag

description.summary: begin a Core-authoritative drag for a Shell tab

request.description: button and serial identify the Shell pointer press that initiated the drag. Core owns layout/drop commit; Shell may provide semantic tab strip targets with set_window_drag_target.

description.summary: begin a Core-authoritative drag for a Shell Group control

request.name: set_window_drag_target

description.summary: supply semantic target for a Shell-owned tab strip

request.description: This hint is accepted only during a Shell-origin window drag. Core still owns layout-edge classification. A hint is used only while the pointer is over a Group-attached Shell surface of the target Group.

event.name: drag_surface_motion

description.summary: report pointer motion over a Group-attached Shell surface during Shell drag

event.description: Empty group_id means the pointer is not over a Group-attached Shell surface. Coordinates are local to the attached surface rectangle. Shell may use them to compute a semantic tab-strip target and send set_window_drag_target.

interface.name: onyrion_group_surface_v1

description.summary: Shell-owned surface attached to an Onyrion Group

interface.description: Placement is relative to the Group outer geometry and is entirely controlled by the Shell. Content insets are configured separately on onyrion_shell_unstable_v1.

entry.name: invalid_rect
entry.summary: surface rectangle has invalid size

entry.name: invalid_layer
entry.summary: surface layer is invalid

description.summary: set relative Group coordinates and clipping rectangle

request.name: set_layer

description.summary: set Shell-selected stacking relation to active Group client

request.description: Core does not choose whether Group UI is above or below client content. The surface remains disabled until this request is received.

event.name: configure

description.summary: report authoritative Group outer dimensions

event.description: Width and height are the current Group outer_box dimensions before Shell-defined content insets are applied. Position-only changes do not require this event.
